Module io.github.brantunger.unruly.core
Package io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.language

Interface CompileContext

public sealed interface CompileContext
What every compilation of a rule list is given: the imports the engine was built with, from RulesEngineBuilder.imports(String...), the class loader to look classes up with, the type of the output object, this language's options, and a way to report warnings. A language uses what it needs and ignores the rest.

Implemented by the engine, which passes it to a language. It's sealed, so a language can't implement it; a language's unit tests create one with io.github.brantunger.unruly.test.LanguageTestContexts, from the unruly-engine-test artifact. Because only the engine implements it, a later release can add methods to it without breaking languages.

    • outputType

      Class<?> outputType()
      Returns the type of the output object, which the engine was built with through RulesEngineBuilder.outputType(Class). A language may use it, for example to check the properties its actions return; the engine doesn't.
      Returns:
      The output type, or Object if the engine wasn't told one

    • declaredFacts

      Map<String,Class<?>> declaredFacts()
      Returns the facts the engine was declared with, through RulesEngineBuilder.fact(String, Class), by fact name. A language may check its expressions against them, for example to reject a misspelled property when the rules load, or ignore them; the engine checks a run's values against them whatever the language does. A fact declared with a primitive type, such as int, is given as its wrapper, Integer.

      A declared type is what a run's value must be an instance of. It isn't a promise that the fact is present, unless allFactsDeclared() is true.

      Returns:
      The declared type of each fact, by name, empty if the engine was told none; unmodifiable

    • allFactsDeclared

      boolean allFactsDeclared()
      Returns whether a run may supply only the facts in declaredFacts(), which the engine was told with RulesEngineBuilder.requireDeclaredFacts(). When it's true, every name a rule can legitimately refer to is declared, so a language may reject an expression that refers to anything else. When it's false, a run may supply facts nobody declared, so an undeclared name isn't a mistake.
      Returns:
      true if every fact a run may supply is declared

    • options

      Map<String,String> options()
      Returns this language's options, set with RulesEngineBuilder.option(String, String, String). What an option means is up to the language.
      Returns:
      The values by option name, empty if this language was given none; unmodifiable

    • warn

      void warn(Expression source, InvalidExpressionException.Issue issue)
      Reports a problem that doesn't stop an expression compiling, such as use of a deprecated function. The engine logs it at WARN, naming the rule, whether the expression is its condition or its action, and where the problem is, and loading carries on. While the rules are only validated, with RulesEngine.validate(java.util.List), the warning is discarded. To stop the expression compiling, throw an InvalidExpressionException instead.
      Parameters:
      source - The expression the problem is in
      issue - The problem, reported as a warning whatever its severity
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if source or issue is null
